findings.claim: The ms→ticks conversion (round up to whole sim ticks) is written twice in the UI: as a private `msToTicks` helper in race-ui.ts and again inline for GO_GONE_TICKS in countdown.ts. Its inverse `ticksToMs` already lives in format.ts, and both files already depend on TICK_HZ for this one job.
findings.evidence:
src/ui/race-ui.ts:21 `const msToTicks = (ms: number): number => Math.ceil((ms * TICK_HZ) / 1000);` (used at :23 and :24 for NEW_BEST_BACK_TICKS / NEW_BEST_GONE_TICKS)
src/ui/countdown.ts:17 `export const GO_GONE_TICKS = Math.ceil((GO_GONE_MS * TICK_HZ) / 1000);`
src/ui/format.ts:5 `export const ticksToMs = (ticks: number): number => (ticks * 1000) / TICK_HZ;` (format.ts:2 already imports TICK_HZ; race-ui.ts:8 already imports ticksToMs from it). A grep for `msToTicks` finds no test or harness importer; the tests only pin the GO_GONE_TICKS value (tests/render/countdown-framing.test.ts:52), which doesn't change.
findings.suggestedFix: Move `msToTicks` into src/ui/format.ts next to ticksToMs, as `/** Sim ticks covering ms, rounded up. */ export const msToTicks = (ms: number): number => Math.ceil((ms * TICK_HZ) / 1000);`. Import it in race-ui.ts (add to the existing `./format.ts` import, delete line 21) and in countdown.ts, where line 17 becomes `export const GO_GONE_TICKS = msToTicks(GO_GONE_MS);`. Both sites run the exact same expression, so every tick constant stays identical. Open PR #31 (HUD event motion) may touch race-ui.ts; apply after it lands if so.

findings.claim: The 844×390 reference frame is hard-coded as bare numbers 7 times across three render modules, though tokens.safeArea.frame already holds it and src/ui/layout.ts reads it from there. These are also raw pixel sizes in src/, which CLAUDE.md forbids, so the next render night is likely to copy the pattern.

src/render/camera.ts:85 `export function createCameraRig(width = 844, height = 390): CameraRig {`
src/render/materials/index.ts:147 `const resolution = { value: new Vector2(844, 390) };` :173 `widthPx.value = (OUTLINE_PX_AT_844 * Math.max(1, bufferWidth)) / 844;`
The single source: guardrails/generated/tokens.ts:219-222 `"safeArea": { "frame": [844, 390]`, read in src/ui/layout.ts:6 `const [frameW, frameH] = tokens.safeArea.frame;`. src/render/car.ts:10 already imports `tokens` from '@tokens', so render may use it.
findings.suggestedFix: Read the frame from tokens once: export `export const [FRAME_W, FRAME_H] = tokens.safeArea.frame;` (or a `REFERENCE_FRAME` pair) from src/render/camera.ts, which gets a `tokens` import. Use it for createCameraRig's defaults, then import it in scene.ts (lines 140, 141, 213, 214) and materials/index.ts (lines 147, 173). The numbers are the same, so camera, outline width and scene stay bit-identical. Keep the OUTLINE_PX_AT_844 name and its comments as they are.
